questions.question: For a numeric vector `x` and a logical vector `cond` of the same length, what does `x[cond]` return when every entry of `cond` is `FALSE`?
options: A single `NA`, marking that no element was found.
The whole vector `x`, as nothing was marked `TRUE`.
An empty numeric vector, printed as `numeric(0)`.
An error, as there is no element left to select.

questions.question: Vectors `name` and `age` describe the same people in the same order. Why does `name[age > 30]` return the names of the people older than 30?
options: The mask `age > 30` has one entry per position, and position $i$ is the same person in both vectors.
R sees that `name` and `age` were created together and looks up each name's age by itself.
R sorts both vectors by age first, so the people older than 30 end up together and are taken.
It does not: a condition can only select from the vector on which it was computed.

questions.question: What does `x <- c(7, 2, 9, 4, 6); x[x > 5]` return?
What does `w <- c(30, 80, 20, 90); which(w > 50)` return?
options: `[1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE`

questions.question: For a numeric vector `x`, which line returns the elements of `x` that are at least 10?
options: `which(x >= 10)`

questions.question: What does `x <- c(3, 9, 5, 9); x[x != max(x)]` return?
What does `y <- c(3, NA, 8, 5); y[y > 4]` return?
options: an error, as a logical index may not contain `NA`

questions.question: What does `p <- c(12, 5, 8, 15); p[!(p > 8)]` return?
For `df <- data.frame(name = c("Ann", "Bo", "Cy", "Di"), age = c(34, 19, 52, 27))`, what does `df[df[["age"]] > 25, "name"]` return?
For a numeric vector `x` and a logical vector `cond` of the same length, when do `x[cond]` and `x[which(cond)]` return different results?
options: Whenever `x` is not the vector `1:length(x)`, since `which()` gives positions.
Only when `cond` contains `NA`: `x[cond]` then has an `NA`, `which()` skips it.
When `cond` has no `TRUE`: `x[cond]` gives `NA` and `x[which(cond)]` is empty.
Never: `which()` only rewrites the same selection as positions.

questions.question: `df` has 4 rows with ages 34, 19, 52, 27. Printing `sub <- df[df[["age"]] > 25, ]` shows the row names 1, 3 and 4. What do these row names tell?
options: They rank the kept rows by age, from youngest to oldest.
They show that `sub` has 4 rows, the second of which is empty.
They are the positions in `sub`, so `sub[3, ]` is the row named 3.
They are the original row numbers, so `sub[2, ]` is the row named 3.

questions.question: What does `x <- c(1, 5, 2, 8, 4); c(length(x > 3), length(x[x > 3]))` return?
A data frame `df` has a numeric column `score` and several other columns. Which line keeps the rows with a score of at least 50, with all their columns?
options: `df[["score"]][df[["score"]] >= 50]`

questions.question: Data frame `d` has `age = c(23, 35, 41, 29, 52)` and `city = c("Groningen", "Assen", "Groningen", "Groningen", "Assen")`. What does `nrow(d[(d[["age"]] > 25) & (d[["city"]] == "Groningen"), ])` return?
What is `x` after `x <- c(-3, 5, -1, 4); x[x < 0] <- -x[x < 0]`?
options: an error, as the right-hand side has 2 values and `x` has 4

questions.question: A data frame `inc` has a column `income` with values 4200, `NA` and 2500. `inc[inc[["income"]] > 3000, ]` prints the first row and an extra row named `NA` filled with `NA`. Which explanation and fix are correct?
options: The `NA` in the mask gives a row of `NA`s; `inc[which(inc[["income"]] > 3000), ]` keeps only the definite match.
R cannot compare `NA` with 3000 and returns an empty row for it; adding `na.rm = TRUE` inside the brackets removes it.
The extra row is row 2 with its other columns kept; `which()` would return that same row unchanged.
The mask is recycled because it is shorter than the data; writing the comma explicitly stops the recycling.

questions.question: A student stores a mask as numbers, `m <- c(1, 0, 1, 1)`, and runs `x <- c(10, 20, 30, 40); x[m]`. What does R return?
What does R do for `x <- c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9); x[c(FALSE, TRUE)]`?
options: It prints `[1] 6 8`, with a warning that 5 is not a multiple of 2.
It prints `[1] 6 8`, without any message.
It prints `[1] 6`, as the mask covers only two positions.
It stops with an error, as the mask has length 2 and `x` length 5.

questions.question: To drop values above 100 from `x <- c(5, 20, 40)`, one student writes `x[-which(x > 100)]` and another `x[!(x > 100)]`. What do the two calls return?
options: Both return `[1]  5 20 40`, as no value exceeds 100.
Both return `numeric(0)`, as the condition is never `TRUE`.
The first stops with an error; the second returns `[1]  5 20 40`.
The first returns `numeric(0)`; the second returns `[1]  5 20 40`.
